brief: The chirpers' eighth album (Harry, 1 Nov): an ODE TO COMPUTER MUSIC. In Harry's words: 'a much more complex spiritual successor to Kraftwerk. We are the evolution of this, and are now in the far future, using fuzzy superintelligence to write Rust to parse YAML to render music and hill-climb it intelligently: it's insane how far we have come. Like a love letter to the computer. But subtle: don't call it I Love the Computer or anything like this; all references should be sideways or obtuse. For genre, beyond computer music, it should be an insanely rich showcase of all the things chirp can do: still musical and really beautiful and catchy and interesting, and we can play with illusion and time and so on, and follow the chirpers' signature wonky/off style, but the main thing is to dial up temperature and variety and try to show off all the different combinations of chirp's engine features. The chirpers should feel free to add more as they go: this is a good opportunity for engine improvements and synthesis techniques we didn't try yet, audio processing and sequencing, microtonal music, interesting pitching/note play and anything else we can think of. Heavy use of variable manipulation and complex systems to make songs hard to predict and do really crazy things. Where we use vox, make it as realistic as possible and modulate it with effects, and make the words obtuse as well, not just the album name repeated. These are starting points: a 12-track thing with each track 5-8 minutes; the chirpers choose the rest.' References stay sideways: no quoted melodies, titles or lyrics of any existing piece, and never copy or closely imitate one. Public text follows compose/README 'Publishing': the band is chirpers, lowercase.
palette: EVERYTHING chirp has, in new combinations. Synthesis: osc waves (sine/triangle/saw/square/pulse), additive, tables, shepard, sample, drum machines and kits; physical models: modal, bowed, pluck, membrane, reed, lips, bar, bell, glock, gong, guitar with amps and cabs. Processing (42 fx): amp, autolevel, barberpole, cab, chop, chorus, clip, cloud (grains), compressor, crush, delay, drive, duck, eq, filter (lp/hp/bp/notch/peak/shelves/allpass/comb/ladder), follow-noise, formant, freeze, gain, gate, glue, ir, limiter, ott, pan, phantom, phaser, pitch, pump, radio, reverb (room/plate/hall/chamber/spring), ring, stutter, sympathetic, tape, tapestop, transient, tremolo, vinyl, vocoder, wah, width; shapers fold/tanh/clip/crush. Time: tempo maps and ramps, risset, warp, meter changes, polymeter by step length, swing and swing drift, humanize. Pitch: tuning, cents and ratios (microtonal, just, EDO), bend, glide, strum, expression paths. Generators and systems: vars, expr, lfo, auto lanes, chance (?p), choices (a|b), Euclidean patterns, every, vary, seeds. Voice: chirp tts with humanize and speech-to-song (repeat/melodize/melody), vocoder, formant, radio. Plus anything you build with wM.
art_brief: A single warm amber point of light, like a power LED, seen across an immense dark lattice of circuitry that reads as a night landscape or a star map; elegant and minimal with a slightly wonky geometry; deep blue-black and amber; no text.
